Confirmed to carry MK items, e.g. the Republic of North Macedonia National Digital Identity Service launch (Nov 2021) which names NLB Banka Skopje as first user and Evrotrust as operator - a bank-technology fact no MK bank published itself.

candidates.source_name: Visa Inc. investor/press release hub (visa.gcs-web.com) and corporate.visa.com newsroom

negative_findings.description: No Visa country newsroom or Macedonian-language Visa press page for North Macedonia was found. Searches in both en and mk returned only Visa global/regional newsrooms and MK bank product pages carrying Visa branding.
negative_findings.result_summary: Visa MK announcements, if any, appear to be routed through issuing banks and local media rather than a Visa-owned MK channel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-side coverage for Visa in MK must be built bottom-up from issuer pages and MK media; a Visa-domain crawl alone will under-report.

negative_findings.description: Targeted searching for MK bank customers of the large global core-banking and self-service vendors (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Euronet, BPC, OpenWay) surfaced no MK-named press release or case study.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic product/comparison pages and third-party customer databases returned; no MK deployment named.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Core-banking platform ownership for MK banks remains unmapped; this is the single largest hole in the vendor picture and likely needs procurement notices, RFP archives, or job-ad/skills evidence instead of vendor marketing.

negative_findings.description: Macedonian-language searching for vendor references ('референци', 'решение', 'соопштение' + Македонија + банка) mostly returned legal texts, registry/company-profile aggregators and chamber listings rather than vendor case studies.
negative_findings.result_summary: Regional vendors publish in English; MK-language material about them is produced by media and directories, not by the vendors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language crawling should be pointed at MK media and associations for vendor news, while vendor-owned collection stays English - splitting the pipeline by language accordingly.

negative_findings.description: Printec's MK country page was located but no MK-specific press release feed was identified in this pass; only a group-level blog and resources library.
negative_findings.result_summary: MK customer facts appear as prose on the country page rather than as dated releases.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Undated marketing prose cannot anchor a timeline; deployment dates for MK self-service estates will need corroboration from another source class.

coverage_gaps.description: Only a handful of the ~13 MK banks appear anywhere in vendor material: NLB Banka Skopje, Komercijalna Banka, Stopanska Banka, Halkbank. Sparkasse Bank, ProCredit, TTK, Centralna kooperativna, Silk Road, Development Bank and others have no vendor-side trace found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a per-bank sweep pairing each bank's official and transliterated name with vendor/scheme terms in both mk and en, rather than vendor-first searching.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM/self-service hardware vendors (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, GRG, Hyosung) and their MK distributors are essentially unmapped beyond Printec.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vendor partner-locator pages and MK Central Registry for local distributor entities; check ATM fleet branding evidence via bank fee schedules and photos.

coverage_gaps.description: Confirmed MK scheme/vendor items cluster in 2020-2021 (Mastercard digital ID, Halkbank wallet) with only a few recent MK-media items. 2023-2026 vendor activity is under-covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add date-restricted sweeps for 2024-2026 across the vendor and MK-media source set, and check whether vendor newsrooms paginate beyond the first page.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor and scheme LinkedIn/Facebook pages (Nextsense, ASEE Macedonia, CaSys, Printec MK) were seen in results but not assessed as sources; in MK these carry deployment announcements that never reach the corporate site.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate social channels as a distinct source class with an explicit ToS/legal review before any automated collection.

coverage_gaps.description: No vendor-side route was found into private-bank procurement decisions beyond voluntary marketing; state-owned or state-adjacent institutions (Development Bank of North Macedonia) may publish tenders that name banking-technology vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-link this cell with the public-procurement cell so tender awards can corroborate vendor claims and fill the core-banking gap.

brief: For North Macedonia, the schemes and vendors are a genuinely productive indirect route: Mastercard's Europe newsroom carries MK country announcements (the 2021 national digital ID launch names NLB Banka Skopje and operator Evrotrust), while Entrust, Netcetera and Nextsense each publish named MK bank deployments - Komercijalna Banka card issuance and online banking, Halkbank's tokenised wallet - that the banks themselves never announced. Visa, by contrast, has no MK-facing channel; its MK footprint is only visible through issuer product pages in Macedonian and through MK business media, which is also where Mastercard's local partnership announcements with Stopanska Banka and Komercijalna Banka actually appear. The domestic layer - CaSys as the sole certified card processor and KIBS as clearing house and CA - is the highest-value indirect source set, since almost every card and payment change in the market passes through them. The principal hole is core banking: no MK bank was found named in any Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR, Euronet, BPC or OpenWay material, so platform ownership will have to be reached through procurement records or per-bank sweeps rather than vendor marketing.
